presentation.summary: Plan and manage outdoor work when heat, workload and worker acclimatization create increasing risk.
presentation.situation: A maintenance crew is scheduled for physically demanding outdoor work during a period of high heat. One worker recently returned after time away.
presentation.objective: Make five professional safety decisions as conditions change.
knownFacts: A maintenance crew is scheduled for physically demanding outdoor work during a period of high heat. One worker recently returned after time away.

work_authorization_record.title: Heat Work Readiness Review
work_authorization_record.summary: The crew is preparing for strenuous outdoor work during high heat, including one worker who is not recently acclimatized.
details: The planned task combines environmental heat with significant physical workload.
A recently unacclimatized worker may have lower tolerance for the same heat exposure than experienced crew members.
Work-rest planning, hydration, supervision and acclimatization status are relevant before strenuous work begins.

control_verification_record.title: Work-Rest and Hydration Check
control_verification_record.summary: Schedule pressure has developed while the crew is due for a planned recovery break.
details: The heat conditions remain elevated even though the job is running behind schedule.
Recovery time is part of the exposure-control plan rather than unused production time.
Hydration, shade or cooling and work-rest timing should continue to reflect the actual heat load and workload.

condition_change_record.title: Heat Illness Symptom Record
condition_change_record.summary: A worker has developed unusual fatigue, dizziness and nausea while remaining conscious and responsive.
details: The symptoms are consistent with a significant heat-strain warning that requires prompt attention.
Continuing strenuous work could allow the worker's condition to worsen rapidly.
The worker's symptoms change the task from routine heat management to an individual health-response situation.

response_record.title: Heat Emergency Response Record
response_record.summary: A second worker has become confused and collapsed during the hot shift.
details: Confusion and collapse are emergency warning signs and indicate a potentially life-threatening heat illness.
Immediate emergency medical response and rapid cooling take priority over production activity.
The occurrence also signals that conditions for the remaining crew require reassessment.

closeout_record.title: Heat Work Resumption Review
closeout_record.summary: The emergency is controlled, but high heat remains and the crew now has reduced experienced staffing.
details: Environmental heat conditions have not automatically improved because the emergency response is complete.
Crew capability, acclimatization and supervision have changed after one experienced worker became unavailable.
Any restart should be based on a fresh work-rest, staffing and heat-control assessment.

safe_completion.title: Safe completion
safe_completion.narrative: The work is completed with controls verified.
safe_completion.keyTurningPoint: The key controls were verified before work continued.

controlled_recovery.title: Controlled recovery
controlled_recovery.narrative: Earlier gaps are recognized and corrected before completion.
controlled_recovery.keyTurningPoint: The team recovered by restoring the control boundary.

major_incident.title: Major incident
major_incident.narrative: Unresolved control gaps lead to a significant modeled outcome.
major_incident.keyTurningPoint: Work continued before the required controls were verified.
